model.name: Position
model.purpose: Model the position as a durable, addressable organizational construct that exists independently of any occupant: the work assigned by competent authority, classified, placed, funded, requirement-bearing and lifecycle-governed, so agents can create, inspect, classify, staff and retire positions without conflating them with people, jobs or contracts.
model.scope_statement: In scope is everything that is true of a position while it is vacant. A position is the bundle of duties and responsibilities assigned by competent authority (5 CFR 511.101) and modelled as org:Post, which W3C defines as a position existing independently of the person or persons filling it. The model owns identity, titling, duty content, occupational and grade classification, structural placement and reporting, location and work arrangement, capacity (FTE/headcount) and funding, requirements and essential functions, delegated and prescribed authority, risk/screening designations, working conditions, lifecycle and effective-dated change, governance and evidence, and outbound interoperability. It does not own the person, the occupancy relationship, the employment contract, the recruiting workflow, or the taxonomies it aligns to.
in_scope: Position identity, keys, official and working titles, and language-tagged alternative labels
Assigned duties, responsibilities and essential functions attributed to the position rather than to an incumbent
Occupational classification, job/class membership, grade or level and job-evaluation outcome
Placement in an organizational unit, cost centre, reporting and supervisory structure
Work location, work arrangement and schedule attributes attached to the seat
Capacity and occupancy control: FTE, headcount, single vs pooled, overlap tolerance, vacancy state
Budget, funding source and the pay range or grade ladder framing the seat
Qualification, competency, credential, screening, clearance and approval requirements
Delegated decision rights and externally prescribed regulatory responsibilities allocated to the seat
Lifecycle states, effective-dated versioning, classification authority, certification, appeal and retention
out_of_scope: The natural person, worker or agent identity that may occupy the position
The occupancy relationship itself (appointment, assignment, tenure, occupancy dates) — owned by WM-ORG-016
The organizational unit as an entity, its charter and its own hierarchy — owned by WM-ORG-002
Team formation and team-level goals — owned by WM-ORG-003
Employment contract terms, payroll processing, absence and time records
Recruiting workflow: requisition approval chain, candidate pipeline, interview and selection records
The occupation, skill and competency taxonomies themselves (ISCO-08, ESCO, O*NET-SOC, NICE) — referenced, not owned
Individual performance appraisal, development plans and remuneration paid to an incumbent
Compensation plan and pay-structure master data (grade ladders and steps are referenced by key)

boundary_notes.distinction: The position persists while vacant; the assignment exists only while an agent occupies it. W3C separates org:Post (independent of holder) from org:Membership, which exists only when an agent occupies a role. Occupancy dates, tenure and incumbent-specific terms belong to the assignment, not the position.

A unit is a collection of people and functions with its own recognition inside a larger organization; a position is a single seat that is contained in exactly one unit at a time via org:postIn / org:hasPost. Unit charter, mandate and unit hierarchy stay with WM-ORG-002.

A position is an instance; a class is 'all positions which are sufficiently similar as to kind of work, level of difficulty and responsibility, and qualification requirements' (5 CFR 511.101), and an occupation is 'a set of jobs whose main tasks and duties are characterised by a high degree of similarity' (ISCO-08). Classifier definitions, code lists and hierarchies are external registries; the position holds only the coded reference and the evaluation evidence.

A vacancy notice is a published recruiting artifact with its own validity window, datePosted, validThrough and application channel; it is a projection referencing zero, one or many positions. HR Open keeps PositionOpening in the recruiting domain and organizational structure with incumbents in OrganizationChart.

W3C org:Role denotes the abstract role and requires a Membership instance to link a person, whereas org:Post is a concrete organizational seat. Role vocabularies (NICE work roles, ESCO occupations) are alignments, not the position itself.

Pay range, grade ladder and budget frame the seat; actual remuneration, contractual clauses and payroll results attach to the occupant's employment relation. EU pay-transparency duties bind the employer's disclosure at recruitment and reporting, not the position record's internal semantics.

sources.title: The Organization Ontology (org:)
sources.relevance: Normative definitions of org:Post ('some position within an organization that exists independently of the person or persons filling it'), org:Role, org:Membership, org:holds/heldBy, org:postIn/hasPost, org:reportsTo and time-bounded membership. Primary basis for position-vs-person separation and vacancy modelling.

sources.title: HR Open Standards — Standards
sources.relevance: Specification families (recruiting, compensation, provisioning, contingent staffing, time, assessments) and the objects PositionOpening, PositionCompetencyModel, OrganizationChart (units, positions, incumbents) and HRMasterData; defines the interoperable exchange boundary for position data.

sources.title: ESCO — Occupations pillar
sources.relevance: 3039 occupation concepts at ISCO level 5 and below, each mapped to exactly one ISCO-08 code, with preferred/alternative/hidden labels in 28 languages, scope notes, regulatory-aspect metadata and essential/optional skills. Source for multilingual titling and competency requirement references.

sources.title: schema.org JobPosting
sources.relevance: Publication-facing vocabulary: title, occupationalCategory (O*NET-SOC or ISCO-08), employmentType, hiringOrganization, employmentUnit, jobLocation, jobLocationType, baseSalary, qualifications, responsibilities, skills, experienceRequirements, totalJobOpenings, jobStartDate, datePosted, validThrough, identifier. Evidence that the advertisement is a distinct projection of the position.

sources.title: International Standard Classification of Occupations: ISCO-08 (UN classifications registry entry)
sources.organization: United Nations Statistics Division / International Labour Organization
sources.relevance: Defines job as 'a set of tasks and duties performed, or meant to be performed, by one person for a single economic unit', occupation as 'a set of jobs whose main tasks and duties are characterised by a high degree of similarity', skill level and skill specialisation, and the 10/43/130/436 four-level hierarchy.

sources.title: O*NET Content Model
sources.organization: U.S. Department of Labor / National Center for O*NET Development
sources.relevance: Six domains — worker characteristics, worker requirements, experience requirements, occupational requirements (generalized and detailed work activities, work context and environmental conditions), workforce characteristics, occupation-specific tasks/tools. Source for duty decomposition, requirement typing and working-condition attributes.

sources.title: 5 CFR § 511.101 — Definitions (Classification under the General Schedule)
sources.organization: U.S. Office of Personnel Management (regulation text reproduced by Cornell Legal Information Institute)
sources.version_or_date: Current text as published, retrieved 24 August 2026
sources.relevance: Legal definition of position as 'the work, consisting of the duties and responsibilities, assigned by competent authority for performance by an employee', plus class, classification and grade. Anchors duty-based identity and the competent-authority assignment act.

sources.title: 5 CFR Part 511 — Classification Under the General Schedule
sources.organization: U.S. Office of Personnel Management (regulation text reproduced by Cornell Legal Information Institute)
sources.version_or_date: Current text as published, retrieved 24 August 2026
sources.relevance: Subpart structure: general provisions (511.101), coverage (511.201–203), classification appeals (511.601–616) and effective dates of position classification actions or decisions (511.701–703). Basis for appeal rights and for dating classification decisions distinctly from record creation.

sources.title: REST API for Oracle Fusion Cloud HCM — Get all positions
sources.version_or_date: HCM REST API version 11.13.18.05, retrieved 24 August 2026
sources.relevance: Operational attribute set of a production position record: PositionId/PositionCode, PositionType SINGLE|POOLED, BusinessUnitId, DepartmentId, JobId, LocationId, FTE, HeadCount, OverlapAllowedFlag, HiringStatus PROPOSED|FROZEN|APPROVED, ActiveStatus, EffectiveStartDate/EffectiveEndDate with effectiveDate query, BudgetedPositionFlag, BudgetAmount, CostCenter, GradeLadderId/EntryGradeId/EntryStepId, validGrades, SeasonalFlag, ProbationPeriod, SecurityClearance, CreationDate/LastUpdateDate.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-181 Rev. 1 — Workforce Framework for Cybersecurity (NICE Framework)
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Task, Knowledge and Skill statements as reusable building blocks composed into Work Roles and Competency Areas that organizations map onto job descriptions and positions; supports treating requirement sets as referenced, versioned components rather than free text.

sources.title: FCA Handbook SYSC 24 — Senior managers and certification regime: allocation of prescribed responsibilities
sources.version_or_date: FCA Handbook, page last updated 10 July 2026
sources.relevance: Requires a firm to allocate each FCA-prescribed senior management responsibility to one or more SMF managers, held by the most senior person responsible with sufficient resources and authority, documented in statements of responsibilities and management responsibilities maps. Primary evidence that regulatory accountability attaches to a designated position.

sources.title: EU action on equal pay — Pay Transparency Directive (EU) 2023/970
sources.version_or_date: Directive adopted May 2023; transposition deadline 7 June 2026; page retrieved 24 August 2026
sources.relevance: Right to pay information prior to employment, prohibition on asking salary history and on pay non-disclosure clauses, employer gender pay-gap reporting at 100+ employees, joint pay assessment triggers, clarified 'work of equal value', and EU-wide guidelines on gender-neutral job evaluation systems issued March 2026.

sources.title: RFC 3339 — Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Internet date/time profile of ISO 8601: full-date, full-time with mandatory time-offset of 'Z' or ±HH:MM, seconds (60 permitted for leap seconds), optional fractional seconds, and the -00:00 unknown-local-offset convention distinct from Z.

sources.title: 29 CFR § 1630.2 — Definitions (ADA regulations), including 'essential functions'
sources.organization: U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (regulation text reproduced by Cornell Legal Information Institute)
sources.version_or_date: Current text as published, retrieved 24 August 2026
sources.relevance: Essential functions are 'the fundamental job duties of the employment position'; factors include the reason the position exists, limited number of employees available, and specialization; evidence includes 'written job descriptions prepared before advertising or interviewing applicants for the job', time spent, consequences of not requiring performance, CBA terms and incumbent experience. Establishes duty-level granularity, essential/marginal distinction and pre-recruitment documentation as evidence.

bundles.name: Position identity and definition
bundles.description: What uniquely designates this position, what it is called, what work is assigned to it, and how that work is classified and levelled.
bundles.rationale: A position is legally and ontologically defined by the work assigned to it, not by its holder or its label; identity, titling and classification must therefore be modelled before any staffing concern.

layers.name: Identity and designation
layers.description: Keys, namespaces and names that let an agent address exactly one position across systems and languages.

findings.name: Position identifier and key set
findings.description: The authoritative identifier for the seat, the secondary business codes that are unique only within a scope, and the external identifiers that make it resolvable outside the master system.

questions.text: Which system is the master of record for this position and what identifier does it assign?
Is the human-facing position code unique globally or only within a business unit or legal entity?
What resolvable IRI, if any, publishes this position as an org:Post in the organization graph?
When a position is split, merged or renumbered, how are prior identifiers preserved and redirected?

data_elements.name: Master position identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier assigned by the authoritative HRIS or position-control system; never a title or a date.

data_elements.name: Position code
data_elements.description: Human-readable code unique within a declared scope such as business unit; Oracle constrains PositionCode to uniqueness within the business unit.

data_elements.name: Published position IRI
data_elements.description: Governed global identifier used when the position is exposed as an org:Post in a linked-data organization graph.

data_elements.name: External identifier set
data_elements.description: Scheme-qualified identifiers used by payroll, recruiting, finance and directory systems, each with the owning system reference.

data_elements.name: Identifier assignment instant
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the identifier was minted, recorded separately from the business effective date of the position.

artifacts.name: Position master record
artifacts.description: The authoritative, effective-dated record of the seat held by the master system, carrying identifiers, placement, capacity and status.
media_or_form: structured record in a system of record
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system position identifier; fall back to governed IRI, then to a Dimension-minted ULID when no upstream key exists.

findings.name: Position title and labels
findings.description: Official title, working title and multilingual alternative labels, including the gender-neutral titling duty that applies to advertised seats in the EU.

questions.text: What is the official title of the position and which authority approved it?
Which working or marketing titles may be used publicly and where do they diverge from the official title?
In which languages is the title published and what are the language-tagged alternative labels?
answer_data: label role such as preferred or alternative

questions.text: Has the title been checked as gender-neutral before the vacancy is advertised?

data_elements.name: Official title
data_elements.description: The title of record used in classification, contracts and organization charts.

data_elements.name: Working title
data_elements.description: Alternative internal or market-facing title that does not change classification.

data_elements.name: Language-tagged label set
data_elements.description: Preferred, alternative and hidden labels with language tags, mirroring ESCO's multilingual labelling of occupations.

data_elements.name: Gender-neutral titling check
data_elements.description: Recorded outcome of the neutrality review required for recruitment under the EU pay-transparency regime.

artifacts.name: Position title register entry
artifacts.description: Governed entry binding official title, permitted variants and language-tagged labels to the position and its classification.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Composite of position identifier and title effective-start date; labels keyed by language tag and label role.

layers.name: Work content and classification
layers.description: The duties assigned to the seat and how those duties place it in occupational and grade classification systems.

findings.name: Assigned duties and responsibilities
findings.description: The decomposed work content of the seat: duty statements, their weight, and the essential-versus-marginal distinction that determines what the position exists to do.

questions.text: What discrete duties and responsibilities has competent authority assigned to this position?
Which duties are essential because the position exists to perform them, and which are marginal?
How much of the position's time or effort does each duty consume?
Which duty statements are drawn from a governed catalogue rather than written free-hand?

data_elements.name: Duty statement
data_elements.description: A single assigned duty or responsibility expressed at task or work-activity granularity.

data_elements.name: Essential function flag
data_elements.description: Whether the duty is a fundamental job duty of the position under the essential-functions test.

data_elements.name: Duty time or effort share
data_elements.description: Proportion of the position's work attributable to the duty; an explicit evidentiary factor in essential-function determination.

data_elements.name: Duty catalogue reference
data_elements.description: Scheme, version and code of a reusable task or work-activity statement, for example a NICE Task statement or an O*NET detailed work activity.

artifacts.name: Official position description
artifacts.description: The certified statement of the duties and responsibilities assigned to the position; also the evidentiary written job description prepared before advertising or interviewing.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Position identifier plus description version number and RFC 3339 certification instant; superseded versions retained, never overwritten.

findings.name: Occupational and job classification
findings.description: Placement of the position in occupational taxonomies and in the organization's internal job or class structure, with each code carrying its scheme and version.

questions.text: Which internal job or class does this position belong to, and is that assignment mandatory?
Which external occupational codes are asserted, under which scheme and version?
On what evidence was the occupational classification determined, and by whom?
What triggers a review of the occupational classification of this position?

data_elements.name: Job or class reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the internal job/class grouping positions that are sufficiently similar in kind of work, difficulty, responsibility and qualification requirements; mandatory in position-managed HCM configurations.

data_elements.name: External occupation code
data_elements.description: Coded occupational category expressed as a scheme/version/code triple such as ISCO-08 unit group, ESCO concept or O*NET-SOC code.

data_elements.name: Asserted skill level
data_elements.description: ISCO-08 skill level and skill specialisation attribution supporting comparability of the seat across statistics.

data_elements.name: Classification decision record reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to the analysis that placed the position in a class, with decision maker and instant.

artifacts.name: Classification evaluation record
artifacts.description: Documented analysis identifying the position and placing it in a class under the applicable classification plan, including scheme versions applied.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Position identifier plus decision sequence number and RFC 3339 decision instant; the effective date of the classification action is recorded separately.

findings.name: Grade, level and job evaluation
findings.description: The levelling of the position and the gender-neutral evaluation criteria that justify it, distinct from the occupational category of the work.

questions.text: What grade, band or level is assigned to the position and under which grade ladder?
Which evaluation criteria produced the level, and were skills, effort, responsibility and working conditions all applied?
Which other positions are treated as the same category of workers or as work of equal value?
Is the evaluation system documented as objective and gender-neutral, and when was it last validated?

data_elements.name: Grade or level reference
data_elements.description: Assigned grade, band or level; a grade groups classes equivalent in difficulty, responsibility and qualification requirements for pay administration.

data_elements.name: Grade ladder and valid grades
data_elements.description: The ladder and the effective-dated set of grades valid for the position, including entry grade and entry step.

data_elements.name: Job evaluation criteria scores
data_elements.description: Ratings against objective criteria including skills, effort, responsibility and working conditions, used to establish work of equal value.

data_elements.name: Category of workers reference
data_elements.description: The grouping used for pay comparison and gender pay-gap reporting to which this position is allocated.

artifacts.name: Job evaluation statement
artifacts.description: Record of the gender-neutral evaluation that levelled the position and allocated it to a category of workers.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Position identifier plus evaluation scheme version and evaluation instant; retained to evidence objectivity of the criteria.

bundles.name: Structural placement and relations
bundles.description: Where the seat sits in the organization, who it reports to, and where and how the work is performed.
bundles.rationale: Positions are only meaningful inside a containing organization and a reporting structure; W3C models both org:postIn and org:reportsTo, and production systems make unit placement mandatory.

layers.name: Organizational placement
layers.description: Containment in a unit and cost centre, and the reporting relations depicted on an organization chart.

findings.name: Unit and cost centre placement
findings.description: The single organizational unit that holds the position, the legal entity and business unit context, and the cost centre that carries it financially.

questions.text: Which organizational unit holds this position at a given effective date?
Which legal entity and business unit govern the position for employment and payroll purposes?
Which cost centre bears the position and does it differ from the holding unit?
How is a position moved between units without losing its identity or history?

data_elements.name: Holding organizational unit reference
data_elements.description: The unit in which the post exists, corresponding to org:postIn / org:hasPost; mandatory department reference in production systems.

data_elements.name: Business unit reference
data_elements.description: Mandatory business-unit scope that also bounds position-code uniqueness.

data_elements.name: Cost centre code
data_elements.description: Financial owner of the seat, distinct from the organizational holder.

data_elements.name: Placement validity window
data_elements.description: Effective start and end dates for the placement of the position in this unit.

artifacts.name: Organization chart extract
artifacts.description: Structural view containing units, positions and incumbents as exchanged in HR Open's OrganizationChart object.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Root unit reference plus as-of effective date and generation instant; regenerated rather than edited in place.

findings.name: Reporting and supervisory relations
findings.description: Post-to-post reporting lines, supervisory span and matrix or dotted-line relations that survive changes of occupant.

questions.text: To which position does this position report, and is the relation defined post-to-post or person-to-person?
Which positions report to this one, and does that make it a supervisory position?
Are there secondary, functional or matrix reporting lines and what do they authorize?
Who acts for this position when it is vacant or its holder is unavailable?

data_elements.name: Reports-to relation
data_elements.description: Reporting relation as depicted on an organization chart, expressible between posts rather than only between agents.

data_elements.name: Supervisory indicator
data_elements.description: Whether the position supervises other positions, which materially affects classification and levelling.

data_elements.name: Delegate position reference
data_elements.description: Position designated to act for this one, mirroring the delegate-position attribute in production position records.

data_elements.name: Relation validity window
data_elements.description: Effective interval for each reporting relation, held separately from occupancy intervals.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Reporting structure is expressed as typed edges between position nodes and is fully carried by the position master record and the organization chart extract; a separate persisted artifact would duplicate those and risk divergence between the graph and the rendered chart.

layers.name: Work location and arrangement
layers.description: Where the seat is located, whether it is remote-eligible, and the working pattern attached to it.

findings.name: Work location and work arrangement
findings.description: Primary and alternate work locations, remote or hybrid eligibility, mobility expectations and any jurisdictional constraint that follows from location.

questions.text: What is the primary work location of the position and which jurisdiction does it place it in?
Is the position remote-eligible, hybrid or site-bound, and who decides?
Does the position require travel, shift work or seasonal presence, and within what bounds?
Which location-driven obligations, such as pay-range disclosure or local labour rules, attach to this seat?

data_elements.name: Work location reference
data_elements.description: Location assigned to the position, distinct from the incumbent's residence.

data_elements.name: Work arrangement code
data_elements.description: Site-based, hybrid or telecommute arrangement as published in job postings.

data_elements.name: Seasonal window
data_elements.description: Seasonal flag with start and end dates when the seat only exists or operates for part of the year.

data_elements.name: Environmental work context
data_elements.description: Physical and environmental conditions of the work setting, drawn from the occupational-requirements domain.

artifacts.name: Position location and arrangement profile
artifacts.description: Record binding the seat to locations, arrangement type, seasonal windows and the jurisdictional obligations they trigger.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Position identifier plus location reference and effective-start date; jurisdiction derived from the location, never asserted independently.

bundles.name: Capacity, funding and occupancy control
bundles.description: How much work the seat represents, how many holders it admits, who pays for it, and whether it is currently filled.
bundles.rationale: Position control is the operational reason positions exist as separate records: FTE, headcount, overlap rules, budget and vacancy state are enforced independently of any person.

layers.name: Capacity and occupancy control
layers.description: Quantified capacity of the seat and the derived vacancy state, including pooled positions with multiple holders.

findings.name: Capacity, FTE and working pattern
findings.description: The full-time equivalence, headcount allowance, single or pooled type and scheduled working pattern that quantify the seat.

questions.text: What FTE and headcount does this position authorize, and are they consistent?
Is the position single or pooled, and may more than one holder occupy it at once?
Is the position full-time or part-time, regular or temporary, and for how long?
How is FTE derived when working hours differ from the standard for the jurisdiction?

data_elements.name: Authorized FTE
data_elements.description: Full-time equivalent authorized for the seat, defaulting to 1 and used to standardize workload across differing hours.

data_elements.name: Authorized headcount
data_elements.description: Number of holders the seat admits; greater than one only for pooled positions.

data_elements.name: Position type
data_elements.description: Single or pooled; W3C also permits a post to be held by more than one person, so single occupancy must never be assumed.

data_elements.name: Employment pattern codes
data_elements.description: Full-time or part-time and regular or temporary indicators attached to the seat, plus any probation period in days.

artifacts.name: Position capacity authorization
artifacts.description: Approved record of FTE, headcount, type and overlap tolerance against which occupancy is validated.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Position identifier plus authorization effective-start date and approval instant; each change creates a new dated authorization.

findings.name: Vacancy and occupancy state
findings.description: The derived state of the seat with respect to its holders: vacant, partly filled, fully filled or over-established, computed against authorized capacity.

questions.text: Is the position vacant, and how is vacancy derived rather than asserted?
Which assignments currently consume the capacity of this position?
What happens when an incoming holder would exceed authorized capacity?
How long has the position been vacant and does that trigger review or lapse?

data_elements.name: Open capacity
data_elements.description: Remaining unconsumed FTE and headcount at an as-of instant; the basis for incumbent validation.

data_elements.name: Occupancy links
data_elements.description: References to the assignment records that hold the post, corresponding to org:heldBy; the occupancy itself is owned by the assignment model.

data_elements.name: Vacant since instant
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant from which the seat has had unconsumed capacity, distinct from the ingestion instant of the computation.

data_elements.name: Overlap validation outcome
data_elements.description: Whether exceeding capacity produced a warning or a hard block, and who overrode it.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Vacancy is a derived state, not a stored assertion: it is computed from authorized capacity in the position master record minus capacity consumed by assignment records owned by WM-ORG-016. Persisting it as an independent artifact would create a second, drift-prone source of truth; only the computation's as-of instant and inputs are recorded.

layers.name: Funding and pay framing
layers.description: The money attached to the seat: budget and funding source, and the pay range that must be disclosable at recruitment.

findings.name: Budget and funding source
findings.description: Whether the position is budgeted, what amount and currency it carries, and which funding source or existing position finances it.

questions.text: Is this position budgeted, and for what amount and currency in which fiscal period?
Is the position funded by an existing position, a grant or a new allocation?
Who authorizes budget changes for the seat and what evidence is retained?
What happens to the position when its funding lapses?

data_elements.name: Budgeted indicator
data_elements.description: Whether the seat is included in the approved establishment budget.

data_elements.name: Budget amount and currency
data_elements.description: Monetary allocation attached to the position with an explicit currency code.

data_elements.name: Funding source reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the grant, cost centre or existing position that finances the seat, including the funded-by-existing-position case.

data_elements.name: Funding validity window
data_elements.description: Dates over which funding is committed, distinct from the position's own effective window.

artifacts.name: Position funding authorization
artifacts.description: Approval record committing budget to the seat for a defined period and source.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Position identifier plus fiscal period and approval instant; approvals are appended, never replaced.

findings.name: Pay range and transparency obligations
findings.description: The pay range or grade-derived pay framing of the seat and the disclosure duties that attach to it before employment and in periodic reporting.

questions.text: What initial pay level or range applies to this position and how was it derived?
answer_data: derivation basis such as grade ladder

questions.text: Must the pay range be disclosed to applicants before interview, and under which jurisdiction's rule?
To which category of workers is the position allocated for pay-gap reporting?
Which pay-related fields are restricted from general read access and why?

data_elements.name: Pay range
data_elements.description: Initial pay level or range for the seat, disclosable prior to employment under the EU pay-transparency regime.

data_elements.name: Pay derivation basis
data_elements.description: Link from the pay range to the grade ladder, entry grade and entry step or to an explicit market decision.

data_elements.name: Disclosure obligation record
data_elements.description: Jurisdiction-specific duty to publish the range in the vacancy notice or before interview, with its effective date.

data_elements.name: Salary-history prohibition flag
data_elements.description: Whether asking applicants about pay history is prohibited for this seat's jurisdiction.

artifacts.name: Pay range disclosure record
artifacts.description: Evidence of the range published or communicated for the seat, with channel, audience and instant, retained for pay-transparency enforcement.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Position identifier plus disclosure channel and RFC 3339 publication instant; superseded ranges retained for the statutory look-back.

bundles.name: Requirements, authority and risk
bundles.description: What the seat demands of any holder, what it empowers the holder to do, and what risk and conditions it carries.
bundles.rationale: Requirements, delegated authority, prescribed regulatory responsibilities and risk designations are properties of the seat that must be determined before recruitment and survive turnover.

layers.name: Requirements and competency
layers.description: Essential functions with accommodation logic, and the competencies, credentials and experience the seat requires.

findings.name: Essential functions and accommodation
findings.description: Which duties are fundamental to the position, the evidence supporting that determination, and how requirements are stated so that accommodation remains possible.

questions.text: Which functions are essential and on which of the recognized factors does each determination rest?
answer_data: factor code such as reason-position-exists or specialization

questions.text: Was the written description prepared before advertising or interviewing for the position?
What are the consequences if a holder does not perform the function?
Do collective agreement terms or incumbent work experience contradict the stated essential functions?

data_elements.name: Essential function statement
data_elements.description: Fundamental job duty of the position, distinguished from marginal duties.

data_elements.name: Essentiality factor code
data_elements.description: Recognized basis: the position exists to perform the function, few employees are available to distribute it, or it is highly specialized.

data_elements.name: Description precedence evidence
data_elements.description: Recorded authoring instant of the written description relative to advertising or interviewing, which determines its evidentiary weight.

data_elements.name: Collective agreement reference
data_elements.description: Terms of any applicable collective bargaining agreement bearing on the duties of the seat.

artifacts.name: Essential functions analysis
artifacts.description: Dated analysis recording each function, its essentiality factor, time share and consequence of non-performance.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Position identifier plus analysis version and authoring instant; the pre-advertisement version is preserved as the evidentiary baseline.

findings.name: Competency, credential and experience requirements
findings.description: Referenced skills, knowledge, qualifications, licences and experience the seat requires, expressed as versioned catalogue references rather than free text.

questions.text: Which competencies are required versus preferred, and from which catalogue and version?
Which licences, certifications or regulated qualifications must a holder possess before occupancy?
What experience level and prior-role expectations apply, and how are they measured?
How are requirement sets kept aligned when the underlying catalogue is re-versioned?

data_elements.name: Competency requirement reference
data_elements.description: Scheme-qualified reference to a skill, knowledge or task statement, for example an ESCO essential skill or a NICE Knowledge/Skill statement.

data_elements.name: Requirement strength
data_elements.description: Whether the competency is essential or optional for the seat.

data_elements.name: Credential requirement
data_elements.description: Licence, certification or regulated qualification with issuing body and any regulatory basis noted in occupational scope notes.

data_elements.name: Experience requirement
data_elements.description: Required prior experience expressed with quantity, unit and any equivalence rule, aligning with published experienceRequirements.

artifacts.name: Position competency model
artifacts.description: The collection of competency information associated with the position or job, exchangeable as an HR Open PositionCompetencyModel.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Position identifier plus competency-model version and the pinned catalogue scheme versions it references.

layers.name: Authority and accountability
layers.description: Decision rights delegated to the seat and externally prescribed responsibilities allocated to it.

findings.name: Delegated authority and decision rights
findings.description: The approval limits, signing powers and decision scopes attached to the seat by competent authority, independent of who holds it.

questions.text: Which decisions may the holder of this position take, and up to what limit?
Which competent authority conferred each delegation and when does it expire?
Do the delegations lapse, transfer or escalate when the position is vacant?
Does the position have sufficient seniority and resources to exercise its authority?

data_elements.name: Decision right
data_elements.description: A named authority conferred on the seat, with scope and any quantitative limit.

data_elements.name: Conferring authority reference
data_elements.description: The competent authority that assigned the work and its associated powers to the position.

data_elements.name: Vacancy authority rule
data_elements.description: What happens to each delegation while the seat is unoccupied: lapse, escalate to the reports-to post, or transfer to a delegate.

artifacts.name: Delegation of authority schedule
artifacts.description: Governed schedule mapping decision rights and limits to positions, with conferral and expiry dates.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Schedule identifier plus version and effective-start date; position-level entries keyed by position identifier.

findings.name: Prescribed regulatory responsibilities
findings.description: Responsibilities that a regulator requires to be allocated to a designated senior position, together with the documentation that evidences allocation without gaps.

questions.text: Which prescribed regulatory responsibilities are allocated to this position?
Is this position the most senior one responsible for the area, and is the allocation gap-free across the firm?
Is the responsibility shared or split with other positions, and on what justification?
Which statement of responsibilities and responsibilities map record this allocation?

data_elements.name: Prescribed responsibility allocation
data_elements.description: Regulator-defined responsibility allocated to the designated function held through this position.

data_elements.name: Regulated function designation
data_elements.description: The designated senior management or controlled function that this position corresponds to.

data_elements.name: Allocation justification
data_elements.description: Recorded reasoning that the holder is the most senior person responsible with sufficient resources and authority.

artifacts.name: Statement of responsibilities and responsibilities map
artifacts.description: Documents recording which responsibilities are allocated to which senior position and how governance responsibilities are distributed firm-wide.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Firm reference plus position identifier plus version and RFC 3339 effective instant; every reallocation produces a new version.

layers.name: Risk, screening and working conditions
layers.description: Pre-occupancy screening and clearance demands, and the physical and environmental conditions of the seat.

findings.name: Screening, clearance and approval requirements
findings.description: Requirements that must be satisfied about any prospective holder because of what the seat can access or decide, determined before recruitment begins.

questions.text: What clearance, vetting or background screening level does this position require?
Does occupancy require prior regulatory approval or fitness assessment of the individual?
Which systems, data classifications or facilities does the seat inherently access?
What happens if a holder's clearance or approval lapses while occupying the seat?

data_elements.name: Security clearance requirement
data_elements.description: Clearance level attached to the position record and required of any holder.

data_elements.name: Regulatory approval prerequisite
data_elements.description: Whether an individual must be approved by a regulator before holding the designated function of this seat.

data_elements.name: Position-derived access entitlement
data_elements.description: Entitlements provisioned because of the seat rather than the person, supporting role-based provisioning.

data_elements.name: Re-screening interval
data_elements.description: Period after which screening or clearance must be revalidated for the seat.

artifacts.name: Position risk and screening designation record
artifacts.description: Dated designation of the risk, sensitivity and screening level of the seat, produced before recruitment and revisited on material change.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Position identifier plus designation version and RFC 3339 designation instant; prior designations retained for audit.

findings.name: Working conditions and hazard profile
findings.description: Physical demands, environmental conditions and hazards attributable to the seat, which also feed job evaluation as a recognized criterion.

questions.text: What physical, environmental and contextual conditions characterize the work of this position?
Which hazards or exposures require controls or protective equipment for any holder?
How do working conditions enter the job evaluation that levels this position?
Which physical demands are essential functions and which can be restructured?

data_elements.name: Work context descriptor
data_elements.description: Environmental and contextual condition of the seat drawn from the occupational-requirements domain.

data_elements.name: Hazard and control record
data_elements.description: Identified hazard with its required control or protective equipment for the seat.

data_elements.name: Working conditions evaluation rating
data_elements.description: Rating of working conditions as one of the four objective job-evaluation criteria.

artifacts.name: Position working-conditions profile
artifacts.description: Structured profile of physical demands, environmental context and hazard controls attributable to the seat.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Position identifier plus assessment version and assessment instant; linked to the location profile because conditions are location-dependent.

bundles.name: Lifecycle, governance and recordkeeping
bundles.description: How positions come into existence, change, are contested, and end, and how the record is kept and disposed of.
bundles.rationale: Classification actions have their own effective dates and appeal routes distinct from record timestamps; without effective-dated governance an agent cannot reconstruct what the seat was at a past date.

layers.name: Lifecycle and effective dating
layers.description: Status transitions of the seat and the bitemporal discipline that separates business effect from record capture.

findings.name: Position lifecycle states
findings.description: The permitted status values of a seat — proposed, approved, frozen, active, inactive, abolished — and the transitions and authorities that move between them.

questions.text: What is the current hiring status and activity status of the position, and are they independent?
Which transitions are permitted and who may authorize each one?
May a position be frozen or abolished while occupied, and what must happen first?
Can an abolished position be reinstated, or must a new identity be minted?

data_elements.name: Hiring status
data_elements.description: Whether the seat is proposed, approved or frozen for staffing purposes.

data_elements.name: Active status
data_elements.description: Whether the position record is active or inactive, held separately from hiring status.

data_elements.name: Transition authorization
data_elements.description: Role and identity that authorized a status transition, with the authorization instant.

data_elements.name: Abolition effective date
data_elements.description: Business date on which the seat ceases to exist, distinct from the date the record was closed.

artifacts.name: Position status decision record
artifacts.description: Record of each establishment, approval, freeze, reinstatement or abolition decision with its authority and effective date.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Position identifier plus monotonically increasing decision sequence and RFC 3339 decision instant.

findings.name: Effective-dated change and history
findings.description: Version history of the seat where every attribute set is bounded by effective dates and queryable as of a date, with record instants kept separate.

questions.text: What did this position look like as of a given effective date?
When was each version recorded, as distinct from when it took business effect?
Is a change a correction of an erroneous record or a genuine change in the work?
How are open-ended versions terminated and what end-date sentinel is used?

data_elements.name: Effective start and end dates
data_elements.description: Business validity window of a version; production systems use a far-future sentinel for open-ended versions.

data_elements.name: Record creation and update instants
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instants with explicit offsets recording when the version was captured and last modified.

data_elements.name: Change type
data_elements.description: Correction versus substantive change, which determines whether prior versions remain assertable.

data_elements.name: Change reason code
data_elements.description: Governed reason for the change, such as reorganization, reclassification, funding change or appeal outcome.

artifacts.name: Position change history
artifacts.description: Append-only sequence of effective-dated versions and the record instants at which each was captured.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Position identifier plus version sequence; each entry carries both its effective window and its RFC 3339 record instants.

layers.name: Governance, assurance and retention
layers.description: Who may establish and classify positions, how the description is kept accurate and contestable, and how records are retained and disposed of.

findings.name: Establishment and classification authority
findings.description: The competent authority that assigns work to a seat and the separate authority that classifies it, including the split between local and central classification powers.

questions.text: Which competent authority assigned the duties to this position?
Who holds classification authority, and is it delegated or reserved centrally?
Which approvals are prerequisites before a proposed position can be approved?
How are classification decisions kept consistent across comparable positions?

data_elements.name: Assigning competent authority
data_elements.description: The authority whose assignment of duties and responsibilities constitutes the position.

data_elements.name: Classification authority
data_elements.description: The party empowered to place the position in a class under the applicable classification plan.

data_elements.name: Approval chain record
data_elements.description: Ordered approvals required to move the seat from proposed to approved.

artifacts.name: Position establishment authorization
artifacts.description: Authorization instrument evidencing that competent authority created the seat and assigned its duties.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Position identifier plus authorization instant and authorizing party reference.

findings.name: Description accuracy, certification and appeal
findings.description: Keeping the position description accurate and current, certifying it, and the routes by which its classification can be challenged and redetermined.

questions.text: Who certified that the position description accurately states the assigned duties, and when?
When was the description last reviewed and what interval or trigger governs review?
Who may appeal the classification of this position, and what is excluded from appeal?
From what date does a corrected classification take effect, and is it retroactive?

data_elements.name: Description certification
data_elements.description: Attestation by the responsible official that the description is accurate and current.

data_elements.name: Review cycle
data_elements.description: Interval or event trigger requiring re-examination of the description and its classification.

data_elements.name: Appeal record reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a classification appeal, its forum and its outcome.

data_elements.name: Classification action effective date
data_elements.description: Effective date of a classification action or decision, governed separately from the decision instant.

artifacts.name: Classification appeal decision
artifacts.description: Decision resolving a challenge to the classification of the position, with its own effective date.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Appeal case identifier plus position identifier and decision instant; effective date recorded independently.

findings.name: Retention, disposition and privacy boundary
findings.description: How long position records and their evidentiary artifacts are kept, what must be preserved for statutory look-back, and where personal data of incumbents must be separated from the seat record.

questions.text: What retention period applies to the position record, its descriptions and its decisions, and under which rule?
Which artifacts must be preserved beyond position abolition to support appeals, pay-gap reporting or regulatory maps?
Which fields carry personal data about incumbents and must be excluded from the seat record or minimized?
What is the disposition action at end of retention: destruction, anonymization or transfer to archive?

data_elements.name: Retention rule reference
data_elements.description: Governed retention rule applied to the position record class, with jurisdiction and legal basis.

data_elements.name: Preservation hold
data_elements.description: Hold preventing disposition while an appeal, investigation or regulatory review is open.

data_elements.name: Personal data boundary marker
data_elements.description: Marker identifying fields that reference identifiable incumbents and therefore belong to the assignment model rather than the seat.

data_elements.name: Disposition record
data_elements.description: Recorded destruction, anonymization or archival transfer with actor and RFC 3339 instant.

artifacts.name: Retention and disposition schedule entry
artifacts.description: Entry binding the position record class and its artifacts to a retention period, hold conditions and disposition action.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Record class identifier plus schedule version; positions reference the schedule rather than carrying periods inline.

bundles.name: Interoperability, measurement and evidence
bundles.description: How the position is expressed to the outside world, what is measured about it, and how the record's quality is evidenced.
bundles.rationale: Positions are consumed by recruiting, statistics, regulators and linked-data graphs; each consumer needs versioned crosswalks and provenance rather than reinterpretation of internal labels.

layers.name: Alignment and exchange
layers.description: Crosswalks to external classification schemes and the payloads by which position information leaves the model.

findings.name: Classification crosswalks and alignment
findings.description: Declared mappings from the internal job and grade structure to external schemes, with mapping strength, version pinning and known conflicts recorded rather than asserted as conformance.

questions.text: To which external schemes is this position mapped and at which level of each hierarchy?
Is each mapping exact, broader, narrower or approximate?
Where do schemes disagree about this position, and how is the disagreement recorded?
What evidence supports a claim of conformance to any external scheme?

data_elements.name: Crosswalk entry
data_elements.description: Mapping from the internal job or position to an external code, carrying scheme, version, level and strength.

data_elements.name: Scheme version pin
data_elements.description: Exact version of each external scheme applied, since ESCO and occupational classifications are re-versioned over time.

data_elements.name: Alignment conflict note
data_elements.description: Recorded disagreement between schemes about the position, kept instead of silently choosing one.

artifacts.name: Position crosswalk table
artifacts.description: Versioned mapping table from internal jobs and positions to ISCO-08, ESCO, O*NET-SOC, NICE work roles and internal categories of workers.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Crosswalk identifier plus source-scheme and target-scheme versions and publication instant.

findings.name: Exchange payloads and publication
findings.description: The outbound projections of the position — organization chart exchange, provisioning payloads, published advertisements and linked-data graph nodes — and what each is permitted to expose.

questions.text: Which outbound payloads carry this position and which fields does each include?
How does the published advertisement relate to the underlying position and its openings count?
Which fields must be suppressed or generalized before external publication?
How are downstream consumers notified when the position changes materially?

data_elements.name: Exchange payload profile
data_elements.description: Named outbound profile such as an organization-chart payload, a provisioning master-data payload or a public posting projection.

data_elements.name: Total openings advertised
data_elements.description: Number of openings published for the position, which may differ from authorized headcount.

data_elements.name: Publication window
data_elements.description: Posting instant and validity end for any published projection, expressed as RFC 3339 values.

data_elements.name: Position change event
data_elements.description: Emitted event describing a material change with its type and emission instant.

artifacts.name: Position exchange payload
artifacts.description: Serialized outbound projection of the position for a named recipient profile, format-neutral in semantics and format-specific only in encoding.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Position identifier plus payload profile name and RFC 3339 generation instant; content hash recorded for integrity.

layers.name: Measurement and evidence
layers.description: Metrics computed over positions and the provenance and quality controls that make the record trustworthy.

findings.name: Position-level metrics and reporting
findings.description: Counts and rates that are only computable because positions exist as records — establishment, vacancy, time-to-fill, span of control, category-level pay gaps — with defined denominators and as-of dates.

questions.text: Which metrics are computed over positions and what is the exact denominator of each?
Is a metric counted in FTE, headcount or authorized establishment, and are these reconciled?
Which reporting obligations require aggregation by category of workers rather than by unit?
How are frozen, proposed and unbudgeted positions treated in establishment counts?

data_elements.name: Metric definition reference
data_elements.description: Governed definition of a position-level metric including its numerator, denominator and unit.

data_elements.name: Metric as-of date
data_elements.description: Effective date at which the position population was evaluated, distinct from the computation instant.

data_elements.name: Aggregation key
data_elements.description: Grouping used for reporting, such as category of workers, unit, grade or occupational code.

artifacts.name: Position metrics extract
artifacts.description: Reproducible extract of position-population metrics with pinned definitions, as-of date and computation instant.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Metric set identifier plus as-of date and computation instant; definitions pinned by version so figures remain reproducible.

findings.name: Evidence, provenance and data quality
findings.description: Where each assertion about the position came from, how confident it is, and which validations must pass before the record is treated as authoritative.

questions.text: For each material assertion, which source system, document or decision is its provenance?
Which validations must pass before a position is publishable or staffable?
How is a disputed or low-confidence attribute flagged rather than silently corrected?
How are conflicting assertions between the master system and downstream copies reconciled?

data_elements.name: Assertion provenance
data_elements.description: Source reference and observation or ingestion instant for an individual attribute value, separate from its business effective date.

data_elements.name: Validation result
data_elements.description: Outcome of a named validation rule with severity and execution instant.

data_elements.name: Confidence marker
data_elements.description: Declared confidence in an attribute, used where evidence is indirect or contested.

data_elements.name: Artifact integrity hash
data_elements.description: Content hash over the canonical serialization of an artifact, enabling detection of drift between copies.

artifacts.name: Position evidence ledger
artifacts.description: Append-only ledger of assertions, their sources, validation outcomes and integrity hashes for the position record and its artifacts.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Position identifier plus ledger entry sequence and RFC 3339 entry instant; entries are immutable and superseded only by later entries.

functions.name: Establish position
functions.description: Create a new seat by recording the duties assigned by competent authority, mint its identifier and place it in a unit.
inputs: holding unit and business unit references
outputs: position master record in proposed status
preconditions: competent authority has assigned the duties
holding unit exists and is active
identifier namespace is declared by the owner package
effects: a new position identity exists and is addressable
hiring status is set to proposed
an establishment decision is appended to the change history

functions.name: Classify position
functions.description: Analyse the assigned duties and place the position in an internal class and one or more external occupational codes.
inputs: classification plan or job catalogue reference
outputs: occupation code assertions with scheme and version
preconditions: a current position description exists
the classifier holds classification authority
scheme versions are pinned
effects: position becomes comparable across statistics and systems
classification effective date is recorded separately from the decision instant

functions.name: Evaluate and level position
functions.description: Apply objective, gender-neutral evaluation criteria to assign a grade and allocate the position to a category of workers.
preconditions: evaluation scheme is documented as objective and gender-neutral
skills, effort, responsibility and working conditions are all assessable
effects: position is levelled and comparable for equal-value analysis
pay range derivation basis becomes available

functions.name: Set capacity and funding
functions.description: Authorize FTE, headcount, position type and overlap tolerance, and bind the seat to a budget and funding source.
inputs: budget amount, currency and fiscal period
preconditions: budget authority approval is present
capacity values are internally consistent
effects: occupancy validation gains an enforceable ceiling
establishment and budget reporting can include the seat

functions.name: Specify requirements and essential functions
functions.description: Record essential and marginal functions, competencies, credentials and experience required of any holder, using versioned catalogue references.
preconditions: duties are decomposed at task granularity
catalogue versions are pinned
analysis is authored before advertising or interviewing
effects: requirements become auditable evidence for selection and accommodation decisions

functions.name: Allocate authority and prescribed responsibilities
functions.description: Confer decision rights on the seat and allocate any regulator-prescribed responsibilities to it without leaving gaps.
preconditions: the position is sufficiently senior for the responsibilities
gap analysis across the firm has been performed
effects: accountability is attributable to a designated seat independent of turnover
vacancy behaviour for each delegation is defined

functions.name: Designate risk and screening requirements
functions.description: Determine the clearance, vetting, regulatory approval and access requirements that attach to the seat before recruitment starts.
inputs: access entitlements implied by the duties
outputs: position risk and screening designation record
preconditions: duties and access entitlements are known
the applicable regime is identified for the seat's jurisdiction
effects: recruitment and provisioning can enforce prerequisites
lapse handling rules become executable

functions.name: Reconcile occupancy and vacancy
functions.description: Compute consumed and open capacity from assignment records and validate incoming occupancy against the authorization.
inputs: current assignment references and consumed capacity
preconditions: assignment records are readable from the occupancy model
capacity authorization is current at the as-of date
effects: vacancy is derived rather than asserted
capacity breaches are warned or blocked per the overlap flag

functions.name: Amend or reclassify position
functions.description: Apply an effective-dated change to duties, placement, capacity or classification, distinguishing correction from substantive change.
outputs: re-issued description or evaluation where triggered
preconditions: authorizing party holds the relevant authority
effective date does not silently overwrite prior versions
effects: prior versions remain queryable as of their effective windows
dependent artifacts are flagged for review

functions.name: Certify description and process appeals
functions.description: Certify the accuracy of the position description and administer challenges to its classification, applying decision effective dates.
outputs: corrected classification with its effective date
preconditions: the description states the duties actually assigned
the appellant and the matter are within scope of appeal
effects: the record becomes evidentiary
corrected classifications take effect on their own governed date

functions.name: Publish position projection
functions.description: Generate an outbound projection of the position for a named recipient profile, applying suppression rules and disclosure duties.
outputs: pay range disclosure record where required
preconditions: position is in an approved status for staffing projections
required pay-range disclosure has been determined for the jurisdiction
effects: downstream systems and the public receive a governed subset
disclosure evidence is retained

functions.name: Freeze, abolish or dispose position
functions.description: Move the seat to frozen or abolished status and, at the end of retention, apply the governed disposition action to its records.
preconditions: occupancy preconditions are satisfied or explicitly overridden
no preservation hold is active before disposition
effects: the seat stops consuming establishment and budget
history is preserved until retention expiry, then disposed with an auditable record

composition.purpose: Every position is contained in exactly one organizational unit at a given effective date, matching org:postIn / org:hasPost and the mandatory department reference in production position records.
Teams are composed through positions and their assignments; positions remain reusable across team formations and are referenced, not owned, by the team model.

A position is occupied through a scoped assignment; occupancy, tenure and incumbent-specific terms live there, mirroring the org:Post versus org:Membership separation, and supply the consumed capacity used to derive vacancy.

composition.target: Job / class / occupation classifier model (sibling; registry entry not yet identified)
composition.purpose: The class grouping similar positions and the occupational category are external classifier concepts; the position holds only coded references, not the class definitions or hierarchies.

composition.target: Person / worker identity model (sibling; registry entry not yet identified)
composition.purpose: Incumbents are referenced only indirectly through assignments so that the position record carries no personal data of its own.
Alignment target for occupational coding and for the job-versus-occupation distinction; mapping strength and version are recorded and conformance is not claimed without assessment evidence.
Alignment target for multilingual labels, scope notes, regulatory aspects and essential or optional skills at ISCO level 5 and below.
Alignment target for duty decomposition into work activities, for requirement typing and for environmental work-context descriptors.
Ontological alignment for publishing positions as graph nodes with postIn, heldBy and reportsTo edges, and for the vacancy-independent semantics of a post.

composition.target: HR Open Standards 4.5 (OrganizationChart, PositionOpening, PositionCompetencyModel, HRMasterData)
composition.purpose: Exchange alignment for organizational structure, recruiting projections, competency models and provisioning payloads.
Publication alignment for the advertisement projection only; the posting is a time-bounded document about the position, not the position itself.

composition.target: NICE Workforce Framework work roles (NIST SP 800-181 Rev.1)
composition.purpose: Alignment for composing Task, Knowledge and Skill statements into reusable requirement sets that organizations map onto positions.
Supplies the bitemporal pattern separating business effective windows from RFC 3339 record and observation instants, reused by every attribute group in this model.
Adds prescribed responsibility allocation, statements of responsibilities and responsibilities maps for positions in regulated firms without imposing them on all adopters.
Adds statutory class, grade, official position description certification, classification appeal and effective-date rules for public-sector adopters bound by such a plan.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension must name one owner package that is master for position identity, declare the master system of record, and state whether position codes are unique globally or only within a business unit.

The owner package must publish who holds establishment authority, who holds classification authority and which approvals gate the proposed-to-approved transition, since the definition of a position depends on assignment by competent authority.
The owner package must register every external scheme it maps to, pin the scheme version in use, and maintain the crosswalk table with mapping strength and recorded conflicts.
The owner package must declare the retention and disposition schedule for position records and artifacts, and the personal-data boundary that keeps incumbent data in the assignment model.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use one namespace per Dimension and per master system, for example vr:wm-org-004/{dimension}/{master-system}/position/{position-key}. Publish a resolvable IRI per position when the organization graph is exposed, typed as org:Post. Never encode title, grade, unit or date into the identifier, because all four are effective-dated and mutable; codes may appear in a separate human-facing position code field whose uniqueness scope is declared.
registry_links: planning/VERCY-MODEL-RELATIONS.csv for CONTAINS from WM-ORG-002, COMPOSE from WM-ORG-003 and COMPOSE to WM-ORG-016
External registries referenced by pinned version: ISCO-08, ESCO occupations, O*NET-SOC, NICE work roles, HR Open Standards 4.5

canonicalization_rules: The canonical form is a format-neutral record; JSON, YAML, Markdown, HTML, Git, MCP and MongoDB are encodings that must round-trip the same canonical content.
Every coded value is stored as a scheme, version and code triple; a bare label is never canonical and never sufficient for a classification assertion.
Every label carries a language tag; the official title is distinguished from working and alternative labels by an explicit label role.
All instants are RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; business effective dates may be full-date values and are held in fields distinct from record instants.
Collections are ordered deterministically by a stable key so that content hashes are reproducible across systems.
patch_rules: Changes to duty content, classification, grade, capacity, funding or authority create a new effective-dated version; in-place mutation of a closed version is prohibited.
Every patch declares its effective date, its change type as correction or substantive change, a governed reason code and the authorizing party.
Corrections restate what the record should always have said and must preserve the erroneous version with a superseding marker; substantive changes open a new business validity window.
Deletion of history is prohibited; a position is ended by closing its effective window and recording an abolition decision, and records leave only through governed disposition at retention expiry.
A patch that changes classification must carry the classification action effective date separately from the decision instant, since the two are governed differently.
compatibility_rules: Adding optional attributes or new crosswalk entries is a minor change; changing identity semantics, uniqueness scope, capacity units or a pinned scheme version is breaking.
Consumers must tolerate unknown codes and unknown optional fields rather than rejecting the record.
Re-versioning an external scheme requires an explicit re-mapping decision with its own instant; silent code carry-over across scheme versions is prohibited.
Derived values such as vacancy state must never be treated as stable inputs by consumers; they are valid only for the as-of instant at which they were computed.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system position identifier assigned by the HRIS or position-control system of record.
Governed global identifier or resolvable IRI, such as the org:Post IRI published in the organization graph.
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension only where no upstream authoritative identifier exists, recorded together with the reason no upstream key was available.
Never an identifier: official or working title, grade, unit, cost centre, incumbent name, or any date.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All instants use RFC 3339 date-time with seconds and an explicit offset or Z, per the Internet date/time profile of ISO 8601; -00:00 is used only for the unknown-local-offset case and is not equivalent to Z. Event time, business effective date and observation or ingestion instant are recorded in separate fields and never conflated.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts are named wm-org-004--{dimension}--{position-key}--{artifact-kind}--{effective-or-instant}--v{n}, lower-kebab-case throughout, with the instant in RFC 3339 basic-safe form so that lexical order equals chronological order. Version numbers increase monotonically and are never reused after disposition.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Each serial artifact records a content hash over its canonical serialization plus the identity of the certifying or authorizing party. Certified position descriptions, evaluation statements, statements of responsibilities and appeal decisions are immutable once certified; any change produces a new version that references the hash of the version it supersedes.

policies: Position records must remain occupant-free: no attribute of a position may identify a natural person, because a post exists independently of the person or persons filling it and occupancy belongs to the assignment model.

Single occupancy must never be assumed. Concurrency is governed explicitly by position type, headcount and the overlap-allowed flag, since both the ontology and production systems permit a post to be held by more than one holder.
A position may not be advertised or staffed until its classification, requirements, risk and screening designation and any pay-range disclosure duty have been determined and recorded.

External standards are alignments, not conformance claims; a conformance assertion requires named assessment evidence with a method and date, and unresolved disagreements between schemes are recorded rather than silently resolved.
Derived state such as vacancy is computed, timestamped and never persisted as an independent assertion that could diverge from its inputs.
Classification, grade, pay-range and risk-designation fields are governed reads: access is role-scoped and every read of pay or sensitivity data is logged.

read: Read a position as of a business effective date, returning the version whose effective window contains that date together with its record instants.
Read the change history of a position, including superseded versions, change types and reason codes.
Read derived occupancy and open capacity for an as-of instant, with the assignment references that were consulted.
Read outbound projections filtered by payload profile and by the suppression rules applicable to the recipient class.
create: Create a position only through the establish function, with duties assigned by a named competent authority and a holding unit reference present.
Mint the identifier under the owner package namespace following the identity priority order and record the assignment instant.
Create derived artifacts such as evaluation statements, designations and certifications as new serial versions, never as edits.
update: Update only by appending a new effective-dated version carrying effective date, change type, reason code and authorizing party.
Update classification only through the classification authority, recording the classification action effective date separately from the decision instant.
Update capacity or funding only with the corresponding authorization artifact present.
Reject updates that would place personal data of an incumbent on the position record.
delete: Hard deletion of position records or their history is prohibited while any retention period or preservation hold applies.
End a position by closing its effective window and recording an abolition decision with its effective date; the identifier is retired and not reused.
Dispose records only at retention expiry, by the governed disposition action, with an auditable disposition record naming the approving role and the RFC 3339 instant.
Erasure requests concerning a person are satisfied in the assignment or worker model, not by deleting the position.

roles.name: Position owner (competent authority)
responsibilities: Assign and revise the duties and responsibilities that constitute the position
Authorize establishment, freeze, reinstatement and abolition decisions
Certify that the position description states the duties actually assigned

roles.name: Classification and evaluation authority
responsibilities: Place the position in a class and assign occupational codes with pinned scheme versions
Apply objective, gender-neutral evaluation criteria and record criterion ratings
Maintain consistency across comparable positions and administer redetermination after appeals

roles.name: Position control and budget steward
responsibilities: Authorize FTE, headcount, position type and overlap tolerance
Bind the seat to budget and funding source and manage funding lapse handling
Reconcile establishment counts, open capacity and budget reporting

roles.name: Model data steward
responsibilities: Own the identifier namespace, uniqueness scope and crosswalk tables
Enforce canonicalization, patch and retention rules and run validation suites
Maintain the evidence ledger, integrity hashes and conflict records

roles.name: Compliance and regulatory officer
responsibilities: Allocate prescribed responsibilities without gaps and maintain statements of responsibilities and the responsibilities map
Determine risk, screening, clearance and approval prerequisites for the seat
Determine jurisdictional pay-transparency and reporting duties and retain disclosure evidence

roles.name: Consuming agent
responsibilities: Read positions as of a stated effective date and honour pinned scheme versions
Treat derived state as valid only for its as-of instant and tolerate unknown codes and optional fields
Never infer classification, exemption status or authority from a title alone

access.default_rule: Position structural data is internal to the organization by default and readable by authenticated organizational agents at bundle and layer scope; pay, evaluation, risk, screening and authority data are restricted to named roles, and no scope grants access to identifiable incumbent data, which is governed by the assignment model.
exceptions: Published vacancy projections are public for their publication window and expose only the fields permitted by the payload profile.
